title: Chapter 13: Bulletproof Systems

claims.text: A historical ranking can depend on the mixture of market conditions; too few regime transitions cannot establish a reliable cycle forecast.
Diversity of economically distinct exposures and simple adaptable rules can reduce dependence on a particular historical regime, subject to costs and changing correlations.
Liquidity constraints can rationally exclude a market even when a later selected trade would have been highly profitable on paper.
A small order can still fail to execute during a liquidity vacuum; small account size does not eliminate market-wide fill risk.
claims.anchor: no traders to take the other side

claims.text: Evaluate complementary strategies jointly with a common capital and exposure budget rather than selecting each solely by standalone return.
Reject the assurance that acknowledging uncertainty guarantees a program anticipates whatever happens or performs well in every future condition.

assimilation: Diversify within executable liquidity and capital constraints; test the combined portfolio and stressed dependence. Accept missed hindsight gains when they follow a defensible predeclared risk limit.
adversarial_review: The three-class taxonomy and claims that members trade identically are broad untested assertions; fundamental and speculative forces coexist. Aggregation does not preclude persistent trends, and ETF applicability cannot be inferred from an old futures opinion. The dated minimum-capital and software-platform claims are not current specifications. The coffee counterfactual assumes fills, sizing and exit history despite admitted capacity concerns; the displayed chart exits after 65 bars, so it is not an independently specified original-rule result. Its initial stop differs from twice the prose N and equal profit per pyramided contract is an approximation. The combined long/short RAR exceeds either component without a clear shared capital normalization; do not read this as a free diversification gain. More systems bring operational costs and can all fail together. Source dating of the famous gold/silver peak is unverified and not accepted as a trading input. Ecological analogies do not prove that every simple strategy is robust.
memory_delta: Diversification requires distinct exposures, feasible fills and normalized capital. Missed profits do not invalidate liquidity limits. No system is bulletproof; regime uncertainty and crowding remain even with simple rules.
reading_provenance: Read all PDF pages 178-189 and inspected the coffee counterfactual chart.
